Satellites, launch vehicles and a refinery: SNT-TC-1A and NAS 410 in El Segundo

El Segundo packs space work into a few square miles. Boeing's satellite factory, RTX facilities and Los Angeles Air Force Base, home of the Space Force's Space Systems Command, sit inside the city; SpaceX builds rockets in Hawthorne next door; and Northrop Grumman's Space Park campus in Redondo Beach designs, builds and tests satellite structures, including the bus for the Next Gen OPIR Polar missile-warning satellite. On the other side of town, Chevron's refinery, the biggest on the West Coast, keeps a large fixed-equipment inspection workforce busy. The two halves of the city certify NDT people in different ways.

Spacecraft and satellite hardware

Satellite and spacecraft programs build few units, each one close to custom, and their NDT requirements are written into contracts that run from the government customer to the prime and down to each supplier. Where a contract or purchase order invokes NAS 410, the employer certifies its inspectors under a NAS 410 written practice controlled by a Responsible Level 3 (RL3). Some programs accept an aerospace written practice built on ASNT SNT-TC-1A with the customer's flow-down added; others do not. Defense work in particular commonly carries NAS 410 down from the prime, since it replaced MIL-STD-410 on defense contracts. The program documents decide, and two plants a block apart can give different answers.

What changes when you cross town

Refinery technicians spend their days on UT thickness, weld examination and exchanger tubing to ASME and API documents, certified under SNT-TC-1A or CP-189. Flight hardware asks for fluorescent penetrant on machined aluminum and titanium, ultrasonic and bond inspection of composite panels and honeycomb, and eddy current on holes and fittings. The physics carries over; the procedures, acceptance criteria and paperwork do not. The aviation penetrant testing guide shows the gap in a single method.

Questions to ask a South Bay space employer

  1. Does your written practice certify to NAS 410, EN 4179 or a program built on SNT-TC-1A, and under which revision?
  2. Who is the Responsible Level 3, or the Level 3 who owns the program, and what will they credit from my file?
  3. Will I need more formal penetrant or magnetic particle training first? NAS 410 calls for more of it than SNT-TC-1A recommends.
  4. Which specimens and procedures will my practical examination use?
  5. Do new hires start as trainees under direct observation, or straight at Level 1?
  6. Will I receive copies of my training, experience and examination records if I leave?

Whatever the answers, an SNT-TC-1A certificate on its own does not satisfy a NAS 410 requirement. It is evidence the RL3 may weigh.

For test labs serving both sides

Independent labs near LAX often carry refinery and aerospace customers at the same time, and mixing the two schemes is a known cause of audit trouble. A technician certified at Level 2 under both holds two separate certifications, each with its own expiry date, never one combined card. Name the governing standard and revision on every certification letter, keep training evidence at the NAS 410 level (approved outlines, qualified instructors, recorded hours), apply the stricter vision and examination rule wherever the two differ, and plan the switch to NAS 410 Revision 6, released in December 2025. Atlantis prepares and reviews NAS 410 and Nadcap AC7114 audit documentation that your own RL3 approves.

What Atlantis does for El Segundo

Atlantis offers aerospace, space and refinery employers in El Segundo the same three things: ASNT NDT Level III consulting, SNT-TC-1A-based training, and UT, MT, PT and VT inspection. Consulting for aerospace includes written practices built on SNT-TC-1A and aligned with customer flow-down and Nadcap AC7114, procedures, Level I and II examinations and outside agency ASNT Level III services; the aerospace NDT consulting page has the detail. Training is self-paced online with Level III Q&A, simulator practice in Practical NDT, and the hands-on practical at your site, since there is no Atlantis classroom in El Segundo. Atlantis does not provide NAS 410 training, certification, examinations or a Responsible Level 3 for El Segundo's satellite, launch or defense employers. Ask your RL3 before enrolling whether outside training will count toward a NAS 410 certification. Read NAS 410 vs SNT-TC-1A for the full comparison and SNT-TC-1A for aerospace NDT for how ASNT-based aerospace programs are put together.
